sources.citation: Michael K. Scullin, Madison L. Krueger, Hannah K. Ballard, Natalya Pruett, Donald L. Bliwise (2018). The effects of bedtime writing on difficulty falling asleep: A polysomnographic study comparing to-do lists and completed activity lists. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 147(1), 139-146.
sources.notes: Overnight Baylor University polysomnography study (n=57 young adults, 5-minute bedtime writing) showing to-do list writers fell asleep in 15.8 minutes (15.82m) vs 25.1 minutes (25.09m) for completed-activity writers, with greater task specificity predicting faster sleep onset.

sources.citation: Matthew E. Ansfield, Daniel M. Wegner, Robin Bowser (1996). Ironic effects of sleep urgency. Behaviour Research and Therapy, 34(7), 523-531.
sources.notes: Classic University of Virginia experiment showing that participants instructed to fall asleep as quickly as possible under high mental load (John Philip Sousa brass marches) took significantly longer to fall asleep than participants told to sleep whenever they desired.

sources.citation: Daniel M. Wegner (1994). Ironic processes of mental control. Psychological Review, 101(1), 34-52.
sources.notes: Foundational dual-process model explaining how intentional operating processes paired with ironic monitoring processes backfire under cognitive load or stress.

sources.citation: Colin A. Espie, Niall M. Broomfield, Kenneth M. A. MacMahon, Lorna M. Macphee, Lauren M. Taylor (2006). The attention-intention-effort pathway in the development of psychophysiologic insomnia: A theoretical review. Sleep Medicine Reviews, 10(4), 215-245.
sources.notes: Clinical synthesis demonstrating how selective attention to sleep, explicit intention to sleep, and direct sleep effort inhibit automatic sleep-wake de-arousal.

sources.citation: Annika Boldt, Sam J. Gilbert (2022). Partially Overlapping Neural Correlates of Metacognitive Monitoring and Metacognitive Control. The Journal of Neuroscience, 42(17), 3622-3635.
sources.notes: Modern >=2015 human fMRI MVPA study mapping prefrontal and parietal neural representations governing metacognitive monitoring and external reminder offloading of delayed prospective intentions.

sources.citation: Evan F. Risko, Sam J. Gilbert (2016). Cognitive Offloading. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 20(9), 676-688.
sources.notes: Critical theoretical review establishing boundary conditions of externalizing prospective intentions: offloading quiets ongoing maintenance loops only when the external record is trusted, specific, and actionable rather than open-ended emotional rumination.
